mcqs.question: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by:
mcqs.explanation: Whittaker proposed five kingdoms in 1969.

mcqs.question: Binomial nomenclature was established by:
mcqs.explanation: Linnaeus established the two-part scientific naming system.

mcqs.question: Prokaryotic organisms are placed in the kingdom:
mcqs.explanation: Monera contains bacteria, which have no true nucleus.

mcqs.question: The cell wall of fungi is made of:
mcqs.explanation: Fungal walls contain chitin; plant walls have cellulose.

mcqs.question: Organisms that lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known are:
mcqs.explanation: Mycoplasma have no cell wall at all.

mcqs.question: Tobacco mosaic virus was first crystallised by:
mcqs.explanation: Stanley crystallised TMV in 1935.

mcqs.question: Carrot is an example of a:
mcqs.explanation: Carrot (Apiaceae) is a conical storage tap root.

mcqs.question: Potato is a modified:
mcqs.explanation: Potato has eyes (buds) at nodes, so it is a stem tuber.

mcqs.question: Axile placentation is seen in:
mcqs.explanation: Axile: ovules on a central axis; pea is marginal, mustard parietal, sunflower basal.

mcqs.question: Mango is botanically a:
mcqs.explanation: Mango (Anacardiaceae) has a stony endocarp, so it is a drupe.

mcqs.question: Vascular bundles scattered in the ground tissue are typical of:
mcqs.explanation: Monocot stems have many scattered, closed bundles.

mcqs.question: Bulliform cells are found in the leaves of:
mcqs.explanation: Bulliform cells let grass leaves roll up in dry weather.

mcqs.question: The normal life span of human red blood cells is about:
mcqs.explanation: RBCs live about 120 days and are destroyed in the spleen.

mcqs.question: The most abundant white blood cells are:
mcqs.explanation: Neutrophils form about 60–65% of WBCs.

mcqs.question: Conversion of prothrombin to thrombin requires:
mcqs.explanation: Ca2+ is essential for clotting; citrate prevents clotting by binding it.

mcqs.question: The universal donor blood group is:
mcqs.explanation: Group O has no A or B antigens on its RBCs.

mcqs.question: The pacemaker of the human heart is the:
mcqs.explanation: The sino-atrial node starts each heartbeat.

mcqs.question: The bicuspid (mitral) valve lies between the:
mcqs.explanation: Bicuspid on the left side; tricuspid on the right.

mcqs.question: The QRS complex of the ECG represents:
mcqs.explanation: QRS marks ventricular depolarisation; T is repolarisation.

mcqs.question: Trypsinogen is activated to trypsin by:
mcqs.explanation: Enterokinase of the intestinal mucosa activates trypsinogen.

mcqs.question: Fats after absorption enter the:
mcqs.explanation: Chylomicrons pass into lacteals (lymph vessels).

mcqs.question: The normal tidal volume of an adult is about:
mcqs.explanation: About 500 ml of air moves in a normal breath.

mcqs.question: Most carbon dioxide is transported in blood as:
mcqs.explanation: About 70% travels as bicarbonate, formed with carbonic anhydrase.

mcqs.question: The pneumotaxic centre is located in the:
mcqs.explanation: The pneumotaxic centre in the pons modifies the rhythm set in the medulla.

mcqs.question: Birds and reptiles excrete nitrogen mainly as:
mcqs.explanation: They are uricotelic, saving water.

mcqs.question: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the:
mcqs.explanation: Each kidney has about one million nephrons.

mcqs.question: The normal glomerular filtration rate in a healthy adult is about:
mcqs.explanation: GFR is about 125 ml/min, or 180 L/day.

mcqs.question: Renin is secreted by:
mcqs.explanation: JG cells release renin when BP or GFR falls.

mcqs.question: Angiotensin I is converted to angiotensin II by:
mcqs.explanation: ACE, mainly in the lungs, forms angiotensin II.

mcqs.question: The resting membrane potential of a neuron is about:
mcqs.explanation: Inside is negative to outside by about 70 mV at rest.

mcqs.question: The myelin sheath of peripheral nerve fibres is formed by:
mcqs.explanation: Schwann cells wrap the axon to form myelin.

mcqs.question: Balance and coordination of voluntary movements are controlled by the:
mcqs.explanation: The cerebellum keeps equilibrium and posture.

mcqs.question: Deficiency of ADH causes:
mcqs.explanation: Without ADH, large volumes of dilute urine are passed.

mcqs.question: Insulin is secreted by the:
options: α cells of the islets of Langerhans
β cells of the islets of Langerhans
mcqs.explanation: β cells make insulin; α cells make glucagon.

mcqs.question: Testosterone is secreted by:
mcqs.explanation: Leydig (interstitial) cells lie between seminiferous tubules.

mcqs.question: Ovulation in a 28-day menstrual cycle is triggered by a surge of:
mcqs.explanation: The LH surge around day 14 ruptures the Graafian follicle.

mcqs.question: Hydroponics was first demonstrated by:
mcqs.explanation: Von Sachs grew plants in nutrient solution in 1860.

mcqs.question: Which one is a micronutrient?
mcqs.explanation: Mo is needed in trace amounts; Mg, K, Ca are macronutrients.

mcqs.question: The element present at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule is:
mcqs.explanation: Mg sits at the centre of chlorophyll.

mcqs.question: Deficiency symptoms of nitrogen, potassium and magnesium appear first in older leaves because these elements are:
mcqs.explanation: Mobile elements move from old to young leaves when in short supply.

mcqs.question: Conversion of ammonia to nitrite in soil is carried out by:
mcqs.explanation: Nitrosomonas (and Nitrococcus) oxidise ammonia; Nitrobacter oxidises nitrite.

mcqs.question: Denitrification is brought about by:
mcqs.explanation: Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus return N2 to the air.

mcqs.question: The pink pigment in legume root nodules is:
mcqs.explanation: Leghaemoglobin keeps oxygen low for nitrogenase.

mcqs.question: The enzyme that fixes atmospheric nitrogen is:
mcqs.explanation: Nitrogenase converts N2 to NH3 and is inactivated by O2.

mcqs.question: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from:
mcqs.explanation: Photolysis of water releases O2.

mcqs.question: The first stable product of the Calvin (C3) cycle is:
mcqs.explanation: RuBisCO joins CO2 to RuBP to give two 3-PGA molecules.

mcqs.question: The reaction centre of photosystem I is:
mcqs.explanation: PS I absorbs best at 700 nm; PS II at 680 nm.

mcqs.question: Kranz anatomy is characteristic of:
mcqs.explanation: Large bundle sheath cells around veins mark C4 plants.

mcqs.question: Glycolysis takes place in the:
mcqs.explanation: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm in all living cells.

mcqs.question: The net gain of ATP in glycolysis per glucose is:
mcqs.explanation: Four ATP are formed and two are used.

mcqs.question: The end product of glycolysis is:
mcqs.explanation: Glucose is split into two pyruvic acid molecules.

mcqs.question: In alcoholic fermentation by yeast, pyruvic acid is first converted to:
mcqs.explanation: Pyruvic acid decarboxylase forms acetaldehyde, which is reduced to ethanol.

mcqs.question: The respiratory quotient of carbohydrates is:
mcqs.explanation: Equal volumes of CO2 released and O2 used.

mcqs.question: Apical dominance is caused by:
mcqs.explanation: Auxin from the shoot tip suppresses lateral buds.

mcqs.question: The plant hormone that causes fruit ripening is:
mcqs.explanation: Ethylene raises respiration and ripens fruits.

mcqs.question: The 'stress hormone' of plants is:
mcqs.explanation: ABA closes stomata and induces dormancy under stress.

mcqs.question: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed by:
mcqs.explanation: Singer and Nicolson proposed it in 1972.

mcqs.question: 'Omnis cellula e cellula' was stated by:
mcqs.explanation: Virchow said all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

mcqs.question: Crossing over occurs during:
mcqs.explanation: Non-sister chromatids exchange segments in pachytene.

mcqs.question: Tendons, which join muscle to bone, are made of:
mcqs.explanation: Collagen fibres in parallel bundles give tendons strength.
